recipes.name: Nippy Pork Salad
ingredients_raw: 4 teaspoons fat-free creamy salad dressing (such as Miracle Whip Free®)
2 drops hot pepper sauce (such as Tabasco®), or to taste

steps.text: Mix the pork, celery, and green onions in a large bowl.

Combine the mustard, creamy salad dressing, horseradish, hot pepper sauce, and salt in blender. Blend to make a saucy dressing, about 1 minute. Lightly toss the dressing with the pork mixture. Cover and refrigerate until serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Nippy Pork Salad
raw_recipe.description: A nice change from chicken salad or ham spread, this easy cooked pork spread is perfect for crackers or sandwiches, or just to mound on lettuce leaves. It's a great way to use leftover pork from a roast.

review.reviewBody: I am the author of this recipes and my directions did not say anything about putting this in a food processer.We like it chunky so we just cube the pork,add rest of ingredients and mix.Also i do NOT add vegetable oil and I use 1/4 tsp half salt optional and pepper to taste !

I didn't make it exactly as described. I must say that the dressing being equal parts mustard, mayonnaise, and horseradish, was amazing! I did add salt and pepper to taste. But the main thing I changed was that I used onion, red pepper, and celery all finally chopped with a mandolin. It came out delicious!

I had about one cup of leftover pork loin chops left so I cut the recipe in half, I did chop in my food processor. Used a sweet onion, Hellmann's mayo, 1 1/2 dijon mustard & a teaspoon of horseradish. I would definitely make them again. I hate to waste food. My husband liked them. Win win!!!

I made this with homemade mayo, homemade fennel mustard and homemade relish! Used pulled pork tenderloin, added red pepper flakes, parsley, celery seed, and onion and garlic powder. Lots pf black pepper. Really tasty. Thinking of adding cream cheese to make it more spreadable or adding egg and bread crumbs to make pork patties, kind of like a crab cake. That makes me think of Old Bay seasoning...

Thanks for sharing!

This is delicious. I didn’t have miracle whip , but used light olive oil mayo. I mixed the sauce in my food processor, then added chunked pork, onions and celery to mix well ( I’m lazy). Perfect way to use up the last bit of tenderloin.

I've made it twice and loved it both times. I tend to stray from recipes once I know it's good and then use them as guidelines. Used avo mayo, added tarragon, added black pepper. I love the spice in it!

This is a great recipe and is just waiting to be messed with. First of all I don't use low fat anything so I immediately dumped the miracle whip for olive oil mayo. Since I had about 1-1/3 cups of leftover pork loin roast I made visual and taste adjustments for the recipe. In place of prepared horseradish I used 4 teaspoons of horseradish sauce. I also hit it pretty hard with Tapatio brand picante sauce as I prefer it to Tobasco. If there is anything I might add to this I would consider using some fresh chopped cilantro to the sauce as I could imagin it adding a fresh flavor to an already great dish.
Quick and easy recipe for using left over pork loin. I doubled the sauce to make it coat more evenly, but the recipe is great.
Very good. Actually, surprisingly so. Will be using this recipe again for sure. Thank you to the submitter for the recipe.
So happy that I have a new way for leftover loin of pork! My husband even liked it!
Perfect way to use up leftover smoked pork loin. I followed the notes left by the original recipe owner and I used real mayo. Nice blend of flavors will definitely make this again
Love the salad Will make it again
Delicious way to use left over pork roast
I had some leftover sliced pork. Served it up as salad on crackers as an appetizer. It was a big hit! Thank you.

I followed recipe except I used white onion bc I didn't have any green onion. I let it meld for 4 hours...then one day and then two days and I didn't really enjoy it for any of these sandwiches. I did like it on crackers the first night. I like all the ingredients, yet I just didn't fall in love with this as a salad, but it was nice on crackers. Sorry but thanks for the ideas..

I like the idea of pork salad but I want to change the flavoring a bit. This recipe doesn't state which mustard to use. I used Dijon but didn't care for the taste. 

I cubed the roast pork I used and wonder if shredding it would be better?

We cooked a Boston Butt yesterday. Today we make the salad. While I really like green onions, many in my tribe do not especially the next day, so I left out the onions. Regardless, it was delicious. I've tried with saltines, other crackers and in a sandwich, but the best is just a salad on the side. Hey, I put green onions on mine. Really great!
